title: Six poster variations
slide_intent: Demonstrate flexibility within a recognizable structure, because consistency should support different artworks rather than force identical compositions.
strategic_value: Repeated vertical logos and heading zones can connect MoMA posters while allowing varied artwork scales and placements.
demonstration: Six posters form a grid of three columns and two rows. Their artwork colors, image extents, logo sides and programme-block positions vary within a related composition.
practical_value: Compare which structural relationships remain stable when image scale and column placement change.

content_islands.name: Upper comparison row
content_islands.spec: Arrange blue, multicolored and yellow/red artwork posters across the top; preserve their different image sizes and signature positions.

content_islands.name: Lower comparison row
content_islands.spec: Arrange yellow/blue, dark and red artwork posters beneath; retain the left/right alternation of the logo columns.

content_islands.name: Shared structure
content_islands.spec: Keep the white title zones and narrow programme/signature columns visible across all six examples.

ingredient.name: Vertical MoMA signature column
ingredient.role: Provide a repeated institutional reference beside changing artwork.
ingredient.application: Compare left- and right-side placement and different programme-block heights in the six examples.
ingredient.scope: Observed historical poster variations; no universal side, size ratio or fixed image percentage is specified by this board.

reference_purposes.Expression: Six color and image treatments share heavy vertical signatures and white heading areas.
reference_purposes.Application: The comparison shows several institutional poster compositions rather than one mandatory arrangement.
